_why: THE RULED SET ON THE CANON (user, 2026-09-05, after F105 read the price path): canon4v (the four-rung book built from vanilla, canonised 2026-09-05 with the academy on the regular ladder) with TWO ruled changes — ai_value 1000×3^era on EVERY tiered industry (canon4v: glass and tooling only) and the investment-pool defines (TOO_LARGE_INVESTMENT_POOL_FACTOR 0.9, CONSTRUCTION_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD 0.9, CONSTRUCTION_EXCESSIVE_THRESHOLD 1.5, MAX_NUM_PRODUCTION_BUILDING_CONSTRUCTIONS_SCALED 0.1, LONG/VERY_LONG construction-time thresholds 160/240 weeks; WANTED_COST_COVERAGE ruled OUT). F105 found the private pool hoarding (world 0.48 of GDP at 1935 vs vanilla 0.29 and 0.19 on canon4-je with the defines) beside under-built consumer industries and construction at 0.7–0.8× vanilla's, and glass showing the 3^era lever moves the price path earlier. config/mod_config.canon4v-hai3.json (+ twin). n=2 (user: 'Go with another n=2 in the ruled config'), 1836 → 1936.1.1.

_arms.canon4v-hai3: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.canon4v-hai3.json} — canon4v (57 buildings, 183 technologies, research events §10.69) through make_ab_config --A 2.0 --B 1.5 --ai-steep <all 17>:3 --divisor 0.000125 --ai-defines <the five>; recipes, costs, employment, techs, research events byte-identical to canon4v (verified by field diff: only ai_value, ai_defines and stamps differ)

_delta: vs canon4v-art3 (F104/F105, the measured arm): the academy back on the regular ladder (fine art 40 a level, not 120), ai_value 3^era on 15 more industries, five pool defines added. vs the canon (config/mod_config.json): the ai_value and the defines only.

_predictions.P1_pool: The defines' signature: world investment pools ÷ annual GDP at 1935 below 0.30 (canon4v-art3 0.48, vanilla 0.29, canon4-je 0.19); Britain's below 0.6 (1.06); the USA's below 0.25 (0.46).
_predictions.P2_construction: Construction points delivered ÷ vanilla rises from canon4v-art3's 0.70–0.80 to ≥ 0.95 at 1920 and 1935; total economic levels ÷ vanilla from 0.80 to ≥ 0.90 at 1935.
_predictions.P3_underbuilt: The under-built consumer industries close: British production ÷ vanilla for clothes, furniture and paper ≥ 0.9 by 1900 (canon4v-art3: 0.68 / 0.99 / 0.62) and paper ≥ 0.9 at 1935 (0.57); their 1935 pooled price ratios fall below canon4v-art3's (clothes 1.04, furniture 1.06, paper 1.09).
_predictions.P4_prices: The four decliners stay below vanilla at 1935 (groceries, steel, small arms, artillery pooled ratios ≤ 0.85), and at least three of the twelve non-decliners move to a pooled ratio < 0.95 (paper, tools, furniture the candidates). Failure reading: the ai_value moves the path EARLIER without holding it down late (F105 §3, glass), and the pool spend lands in the untiered sector.
_predictions.P5_tier_choice: Below-best share falls from 44.9% toward canon4-je's 37% (≤ 41% in both runs): the time thresholds stop penalising the ×8 rung in small sectors and the steeper ai_value lifts the frontier's score.
_predictions.P6_gdp_no_stall: World GDP ÷ vanilla ≥ 0.90 in both runs (canon4v-art3 0.82–1.09), the shortlist ≥ 1.15; no stall (the ab-family stalled 1 in 5; more spend is more exposure to the 1860 pool-collapse pattern of F99).
_predictions.P7_wall: Row P inside the 10% budget; a faster-spending pool means more buildings and a bigger world, so the total may move from canon4v-art3's 2.8% faster toward vanilla's pace; P ≤ +5%.
_predictions.P8_academy: The regular-ladder academy's first reading: British fine art 140–165% of base at 1935 (F103's pin; canon4-je 156, vanilla 142), Britain 25–45 academy levels, the film rung the largest where film is held.

_watch: 5-minute smoke check: mod marker, version, this run's error window by POSITION (parsed time), clock, the NAI block in the emitted defines file (six keys), queue_mix at the first summary
first run (before the batch completes): first_run_decomp (GDP = pop × productive/capita × £/productive), pool ÷ GDP at 1900/1920/1935, the four decliners' British prices, tier choice
post-run: preflight -Session (L12/L17/L26/L28), VERDICT.md, SESSION_VERDICTS row, FINDINGS, the ledger
_cost: 2 × 1836→1936 ≈ 2 × 2h40 ≈ 5.5 h on the four-rung book's measured pace (canon4v-art3 runs 147–169 min), plus the harvest.
_caveats: Two levers at once, by ruling. The pool ÷ GDP figure is the defines' signature and the tier/industry allocation the ai_value's, so the two read apart on those; GDP, prices and construction volume do not separate them.

n=2 against a per-run 1935 spread that read groceries 44–101% of base at n=4: single-good price readings are noise at this n; the pool share, construction volume and production ratios are the robust readings.
The academy is the canon's regular ladder here, so fine art is a new reading, not a comparison with F104's ×3 rung.

The construction-time thresholds are ×4 (160/240), not ×8: the ×8 rung is still scored down in sectors under ~240 points a week. If tier choice does not move in small countries, that is the first suspect.
